capabilities: Assign a classification label to notes and attachments
Display classification badges or dots in file explorer and header
Set default classifications per folder and for new notes
Batch reclassify selected files with a preview
List notes with missing or unknown classifications
disambiguation: Not a content classifier; it only stores and displays a label you pick, and other plugins read the property.
extras: Attachment classifications and folder rules are stored in a _meta.md file in each folder, which the README says to skip when reading individual note classifications. Manual install by copying manifest.json, main.js, and styles.css; development requires Node.js 24.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to mark notes and attachments with a sensitivity label and see that label while browsing the file explorer.

relations.evidence: Langdock Sync uses the property to determine which notes are eligible for synchronization

summary: Plugin that saves a classification label in a note's YAML frontmatter and shows it as a badge or dot in the file explorer and note header.
